question: How does resistance affect current and bulb brightness at constant voltage?

en.title: Resistance and bulb brightness
en.summary: Change resistance in a simplified constant-voltage circuit and observe current and power.

copy.title: How resistance affects current and bulb brightness
copy.tldr: At constant voltage, increasing resistance lowers current and dissipated power, so the bulb dims. I is current, V is voltage, R is resistance, and P is power used here to represent brightness.
copy.key_formula: I = V / R; P = V² / R
copy.learning_objective: Explain causally how increasing resistance at a constant 6 V lowers current and dissipated power, dimming the bulb.
copy.misconception: Increasing resistance does not allow more current to flow, but reduces current when voltage stays constant.
copy.explanation_prompt: Use Ohm's law to explain why the bulb dims as resistance increases while voltage stays constant.
copy.transfer_prompt: Predict what happens to circuit current and bulb brightness if a smaller resistor replaces the current one while voltage remains constant.
suggestions: Explore how changing voltage affects current.
Compare series and parallel resistor connections.
Test how electrical energy becomes heat.
copy.brief_summary: Shows how resistance controls current, power, and bulb brightness at constant voltage.
